messages:
alyssa: Heads-up — after rolling the 536.33 driver + CUDA 12.3 stack to staging, we see a kernel-level perf regression for medium seq (129-512). p50 flat, but p95 up ~2.1x for text-gen workloads. KV cache hit patterns look OK tho. Anyone else seeing this?
matt: I saw the same on an h100 pool. It looks like the runtime picked a different attention kernel (fused_attention_v3) for mid-length buckets. Previously it used fused_attention_v2/cutlass fallback.
devon: Profiling data: increased L2 miss rate and a big jump in global memory traffic when the autotuner selects fused_attention_v3 at seq=256. My hypothesis: the new kernel's tile shape and shared memory layout interact poorly with the new driver scheduler, causing more DRAM roundtrips for KV loads.
alyssa: Oof. Do we have a repro run I can paste into perf dash?
devon: Pushed a lightweight repro (batch=8, seq=256, temp=0.7) to perf-runner: run id perf/2026-03-14-18. See flame graphs and nvprof counters. Key bits:
```
- kernel chosen: fused_attention_v3 (autotune)
- sm_efficiency down 15% vs v2
- L2 hit rate from 72% -> 48%
- DRAM throughput +38%
```
matt: Also seeing KV cache eviction churn rise slightly — KV pages getting refetched more often during generation for that bucket. Could be due to different register / shared memory usage increasing context spills.
sre-jen: From SRE angle: customer-facing p95 spikes -> alerts. We should triage and mitigate fast: either force the old kernel for affected buckets, pin driver rollback for the affected pool, or disable the autotuner selection for seq in [129,512].
alyssa: Agreed. Quick triage options ranked: 1) runtime feature-flag to force kernel override for seq ranges, 2) mute autotuner (global off) until we fix, 3) rollback driver (painful). Thoughts?
matt: Prefer 1 then 2. Rolling drivers in prod is heavy. We can add a per-cluster override in the config: runtime.kernel_override.bucket_map = {"129-512": "fused_attention_v2"}. I'll draft the change.
devon: I can add a safeguard to the autotuner: keep last-known-good kernel per architecture + seq-bucket for 24h and don't switch more than once in that window. That would avoid flip-flops during driver upgrades.
sre-jen: For immediate mitigation, propose we: a) set kernel override on the staging and canary pools (apply now), b) schedule a rolling canary to verify p95 returns to baseline, c) if good, apply to affected dedicated pools.
alyssa: I'll trigger the override. Command shipped for infra team:
```bash
# set kernel override for mid seq on the h100 pool (canary)
rdctl cluster set-config --cluster h100-canary \
  --set "runtime.kernel_override.129-512=fused_attention_v2"
```
deploy-bot: deploy started for h100-canary at 2026-03-14T18:40:12Z
infra-bot: config updated on h100-canary (applied by alyssa)
matt: After apply, run perf/2026-03-14-19 to compare. Also add a/ b test: disable autotuner but keep override to make sure nothing else flips.
devon: FYI my patch to autotuner (safety window + perf guard) is WIP: PR #4227. It computes a micro-regression score using L2 hit delta + DRAM throughput delta; if score > threshold, it rejects the new candidate and logs a guarded fallback.
alyssa: Timeline: we need canary results within 2 hours. If revert fixes p95, we keep override and schedule postmortem fix (autotuner + kernel devs). If not, we escalate to driver pin plan.
sre-jen: I'll silence noisy alerts for the affected customers during the canary to avoid alert fatigue, but will keep pager for true incidents.
matt: One more note — the kernel chooser also consults architecture compute capability (sm=90 vs sm=89). The new driver changed some performance counters semantics so chooser's heuristics mis-ranked v3 on sm=90. We should add a normalization step in the autotuner when driver version changes.
devon: Good call. Add driver_version to autotuner profile keys so we can detect when a driver change invalidates cached ranks.
alyssa: Post-canary actions: 1) if good, open a dev task to add driver-aware autotune invalidation + safety window; 2) run deeper probe for seq 64/1024 to ensure nothing else regressed; 3) keep kernel override for 48h, then re-evaluate.
deploy-bot: canary deploy finished at 2026-03-14T19:20:05Z
infra-bot: perf-run update: perf/2026-03-14-19 shows p95 back to baseline on canary (stable fused_attention_v2).
alyssa: Excellent — close loop: keeping override on canary and staging, rolling to dedicated pools tonight. Devon/Matt, please coordinate the autotuner fix PR and postmortem notes. I'll open the incident ticket and tag folks. :thumbsup:
devon: Will do; I'll also add a short repro snippet to the PR so kernel devs can iterate.
matt: I'll schedule a small lab run tomorrow to test fused_attention_v3 under the exact driver/SM combos to debug tile interactions.
sre-jen: Closing alerts, will watch post-roll.
alyssa: Thanks all.
